semantic_correction.stem: A client who recently reported suicidal ideation is preparing for discharge after an evidence-based suicide-risk assessment. Which nursing action best reflects collaborative safety planning?

options.A: Ask the client to sign a no-harm agreement and use the signed promise as the primary protection, while arranging routine follow-up and crisis contacts.
options.B: Collaboratively identify warning signs, internal coping steps, supportive people or places, professional resources, and ways to make the environment safer.
options.C: Provide crisis-line and emergency contact information, then defer individualized warning signs and coping strategies until the client requests additional planning.
options.D: Develop the safety plan for the client based on the assessment, then review the completed plan without asking the client to identify personal coping resources.

semantic_correction.rationale: VA suicide-prevention guidance describes the Safety Planning Intervention as collaborative and patient-centered. Core components include warning signs, internal coping strategies, social contacts or supports, professionals and agencies to contact for help, and making the environment safer. VA MIRECC guidance also states that safety planning and crisis response planning are recommended over no-harm contracts, which lack research support. Therefore B best reflects collaborative safety planning. A substitutes a no-harm agreement as the primary safety intervention. C provides useful crisis contacts but omits individualized warning signs and coping steps. D conflicts with the collaborative, personalized nature of safety planning by creating the plan without the client’s active input.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Develop suicide safety plans collaboratively with the client by identifying individualized warning signs, internal coping strategies, social supports, professional/crisis resources, and environmental-safety steps rather than relying on a no-harm agreement or a clinician-created plan.
semantic_correction.source_organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Rocky Mountain MIRECC for Suicide Prevention; VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline
semantic_correction.source_document_title: The Safety Planning Intervention; Crisis Response Planning and Safety Planning; Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024)
semantic_correction.source_version_date: VA/DoD suicide-risk CPG published 2024 and remains the current CPG listed by VA; current VA MIRECC safety-planning resources rechecked August 20, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: VA MIRECC ‘The Safety Planning Intervention’: SPI is collaborative and patient-centered; Step 1 warning signs, Step 2 internal coping strategies, Step 3 social contacts, Step 4 family/friends, Step 5 professionals/agencies, Step 6 making the environment safe; manual emphasizes provider–Veteran collaboration and personalization. MIRECC CPG Recommendation Resource 7: CRP/SPI are collaborative, patient-centered, share warning signs, internal coping, social support, and professional/crisis services, and are recommended over ‘no harm contracts,’ which have no research support.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Collaborative suicide safety planning is individualized and patient-centered and includes warning signs, internal coping strategies, social supports, professional/crisis resources, and environmental-safety steps; VA guidance recommends this approach over no-harm contracts.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 (official PDF pageno 13): assess psychosocial factors influencing care and plan interventions; provide care and education for acute/chronic psychosocial health issues including depression; promote a therapeutic environment; assess client support system to aid in plan of care; use therapeutic communication techniques.
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — collaborative suicide safety planning after suicide-risk assessment
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the collaborative safety-planning construct and rebuilt A/B/C/D to comparable length while preserving the VA-supported distinction between individualized safety planning and no-harm agreements or noncollaborative plans.

scope_exclusions.acute_emergency: The stem specifies discharge after an evidence-based risk assessment; it does not suggest that a safety plan substitutes for emergency stabilization or higher-level care when indicated.
scope_exclusions.crisis_number: No specific crisis-line number is tested; professional and crisis resources are included as a component of the plan.
scope_exclusions.lethal_means_detail: The item tests the broader environment-safety component rather than a specific lethal-means counseling protocol or method.
scope_exclusions.contract_language: The distractor uses a no-harm agreement as the primary protection; the item does not claim that any supportive verbal commitment has zero clinical value in all contexts.
scope_exclusions.population: The tested principles are safety-planning principles; the cited VA resource is authoritative suicide-prevention guidance and the item does not claim that VA-specific administrative procedures govern all non-VA facilities.
scope_exclusions.blueprint_precision: The cited NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity page does not explicitly name suicide safety planning; mapping is through psychosocial intervention planning, depression/mental-health care, support-system assessment, therapeutic environment, and therapeutic communication.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘suicide safety planning warning signs coping strategies social supports professional crisis resources no harm contract’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Plausible because contracts or agreements have historically been used in suicide care and the option adds follow-up contacts, but VA guidance recommends collaborative safety planning over no-harm contracts as the primary intervention.
option_audit.B: Correct. It captures the collaborative structure and the core personalized components of the Safety Planning Intervention.
option_audit.C: Plausible because crisis contacts are an important component, but contact information alone is not the individualized, stepwise safety plan described by VA guidance.
option_audit.D: Plausible because clinicians use assessment findings to guide care, but safety planning is explicitly collaborative and patient-centered rather than written for the client without active input.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. B alone preserves collaboration plus the core individualized safety-plan components. A elevates a no-harm agreement, C is incomplete, and D removes client collaboration.

cueing_check.note: The key is not the longest option; all four are parallel nursing actions with comparable specificity and no ‘only/always/never/every’ cue.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Collaborative psychosocial planning, support-system assessment, therapeutic communication, and care of clients with depression/mental illness are directly represented in the 2026 Psychosocial Integrity activity statements.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: VERIFIED. No claim is made that the page explicitly names suicide safety planning.
